paras: The Texarkana shotgun threat was an incident on the afternoon of 6 August 1900 in Texarkana in which a white man loaded his shotgun and went looking for a Black man whom his wife said had cursed her. Officers reached the Black man first and took him to jail, where a complaint for abusive language was lodged against him, and the local paper credited them with having saved his life.

According to The Daily Texarkanian, the white man lived on the city's East Side, and his wife told him that she had been cursed by "a negro." The paper gave no names for any of the people involved and did not describe the alleged cursing beyond the wife's report.

On hearing his wife's account, the man "proceeded to load his shot gun and go in search of the negro." An East Side officer and a West Side officer found the Black man before he did and "spirited him off to Jail." No shot was fired and no injury was reported.

At the jail a complaint for abusive language was lodged against the Black man, a charge that matched the wife's accusation. The item reported no arrest or charge against the man with the shotgun, and no report of a hearing or of the outcome of the complaint was found.

The only report found was a three-sentence local item on page 3 of The Daily Texarkanian of 7 August 1900, which opened by crediting the "prompt action" of the officers with having "saved a negroe's life." The paper thus treated the armed hunt as a real danger to the Black man's life while presenting the wife's cursing claim as the cause and reporting his jailing and charge without comment. No other white paper and no Black paper in the coverage carried the story.

bases: A single armed white man set out with a loaded shotgun to find a Black man, and officers removed the Black man before any violence occurred; no one was hurt (A1).

accounts.label: Local newspaper item
accounts.gist: Officers of the East and West Side beat an armed white man to the Black man said to have cursed his wife and took the Black man to jail, where he was charged with abusive language; the paper said their action saved his life.

framing.detail: The Daily Texarkanian praised the officers for saving 'a negroe's life' but treated the wife's cursing claim as the cause and reported the Black man's jailing and charge without comment, naming no one and reporting no action against the armed man.

record_check.record: A white man of Texarkana's East Side loaded his shotgun to hunt a Black man said to have cursed his wife; officers jailed him before he found him.
record_check.dossier: Officers reached the Black man first and jailed him, the Black man, on a complaint of abusive language; no arrest of the armed white man is reported.
The article names Texarkana and its 'East Side' and 'West Side' but no state or county; TX/Bowie is not supported by the text.
Cursing a white woman (her report to her husband); a complaint for abusive language was lodged against the Black man.
The Black man was taken into custody by officers, protectively and on a complaint.
The wife's report that the Black man had cursed her.
